canonical_name: Lanford proof of the Feigenbaum conjectures (repository proof-family label)
literal_source_claim_zh: Feigenbaum猜想的计算机辅助证明
literal_source_claim_en: A computer-assisted proof of the Feigenbaum conjecture(s).
statement_blocker: The catalog gives a proof-family label and one-line description but does not select a numbered source theorem or conjunction. Lanford's matching 1982 announcement states distinct fixed-point, hyperbolicity, unstable-manifold, and quadratic-family transversality results and says it proves essentially all of a family of conjectures. Selecting Theorem 1, Theorems 1 and 3, or Theorems 1, 3, 4, and 5 would be a proposition-changing decision that requires accountable and independent source review.
domain_and_universes: Open: the selected source clause must fix real and complex scalar domains; interval-map and analytic-function spaces; normalization, topology, norms, differentiability and analyticity; the renormalization operator and its domain; derivative and spectrum encodings; invariant manifolds and bifurcation surfaces; and any certificate data and checker types.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not say whether the root is analytic fixed-point existence, derivative hyperbolicity, a bifurcation-surface intersection, quadratic-family transversality, an exact conjunction, or a source-specific computation-correctness theorem.
degenerate_case_status: No boundary case is excluded at intake because no proposition has been selected; the statement phase must resolve every listed case.
candidate_scope_not_credited: Lanford 1982 Theorem 1: existence, analyticity, evenness, fixed-point identity, and negative Schwarzian derivative
Lanford 1982 Theorem 3: hyperbolicity of the derivative with one-dimensional expanding subspace and positive expanding eigenvalue
Lanford 1982 Theorem 4: an unstable-manifold iterate reaches the simple period-doubling bifurcation surface
Lanford 1982 Theorem 5: transversal stable-manifold crossing for the quadratic family near the stated parameter
the conjunction of Theorems 1 and 3 as the core reached from Estimates 1 and 2
the conjunction of Theorems 1, 3, 4, and 5 as a source-suite interpretation
a correctness theorem for an independently specified interval-arithmetic certificate and checker
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: maps on the boundary of the renormalization domain and non-strict variants of its inequalities
critical point, endpoint, normalization, sign, iterate, and composition conventions
real restriction versus complex analytic extension and points on the boundary of the analytic domain
second-order vanishing and the exact analytic-function Banach subspace and norm

strict interval enclosures, finite-precision semantics, roundoff direction, overflow, certificate completeness, and checker trust
excluded_substitutions: the stronger transversal unstable-manifold crossing explicitly described by Lanford as unproved
